_about: The detective's inner voice when a clue breaks a suspect's story. Keyed 'CLUE|suspect.claim'. Shown only in a variant whose claims list that clue in broken_by, and only until that lie is caught. 'mark' is the exact detail to highlight in the clue's text or log; {placeholders} are the case's random variables. Lines hint, they never name the liar. 'press' lists details a player can quote in a typed question to the suspect to catch that lie without showing the card (Engine.press); each must appear in the clue in every variant that uses the line.

D2|ta.proofread_on_screen.line: Strange. A paper exam, printed from a staff card. I thought this one only ever lived on a screen.

L1|ta.proofread_on_screen.line: A staff card at the gate, just before the job came out. Somebody's screen wasn't enough tonight.

L1|class_rep.home_all_evening.line: Card {rep_card}: in at 18:31, out at 19:05. Who carries that card, and where did they say they were?

L3|class_rep.home_all_evening.line: This door had a busier evening than its owner lets on.

D6|class_rep.reported_at_once.line: A first draft at 21:15, hours before anyone could have seen the leak. Interesting timing.

L2|ta.card_lost_at_lunch.line: Straight back in the wallet, the Cashier says. Then how does a card go missing at lunch?
L2|ta.card_lost_at_lunch.mark: put it straight back in the wallet

D8|professor.faculty_dinner.line: So that is who shared the dinner table. Not exactly faculty.

L4|companion.never_went_to_office_door.line: A well-dressed woman at a locked door at 19:40. Lost, she said. I wonder who else will say that.

D1|companion.never_touched_laptop.line: No scan, no print band. Exported on an iPad that signs itself {alias_initials} Whose initials are those?
